description: Real tourist photos of 10 famous buildings from Wikimedia Commons, only files whose own camera EXIF carries GPS (the product's upload rule), up to 150 per building chosen for compass-sector and author diversity, with MegaDepth-X reference poses where the photo is in the reference model. Metadata only: scripts/materialize_testset.py downloads and rebuilds every photo and verifies its sha256.
licence: Photos: Wikimedia Commons, each under its own licence (photos[].licence, licence_url, author, credit; most need attribution, BY-SA also share-alike). Reference SfM models: MegaDepth-X, CC BY 4.0. Outlines (outlines/): © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0. Only metadata is committed; photos and anything derived from them (reconstructions, point clouds, GLBs, screenshots) stay outside the repository.
product_rule: Uploads must be camera originals with EXIF and GPS: every photo here has GPS in its own camera EXIF (as shown in the file's Commons metadata table; nothing simulated or taken from Commons {{Location}} templates). Compass heading and focal length are optional and counted.

selection.candidates: Per building: the Commons category tree of the building (eval/landmarks.json commons_categories; first page of each category, depth 3, subcategories matching collect_params.exclude_category not followed), the MegaDepth-X photos with real EXIF GPS inside the radius (titles source; the curator's ten/mdx_gps_photos.json) and name-matched nearcoord Special:Search result pages the curator saved earlier (search source; no new search requests: robots.txt disallows /wiki/Special:).
selection.screening: materialize_testset.screening_order: files named by several source kinds first, then titles/search/category round-robin; description pages are screened until 225 pass (EXIF table shows GPS inside radius_m, not off-target, at most 25 per author counted) or 600 were screened.
selection.off_target: materialize_testset.is_off_target over the title and the file's own categories: 'views from', observation decks, aerial, interior unless labelled exterior, '... from (the) <landmark>'; such files are dropped.
selection.keep: At most 150 per building and 25 per author (materialize_testset.normalize_author), visited in materialize_testset.diversity_order: within each compass sector (landmark -> camera bearing) round-robin over authors, each author's photos closest first; then round-robin over sectors. A file is kept when its rebuilt EXIF reads back (crowd3d.exif.read_photo_meta) with GPS inside radius_m, a standard-width thumbnail is served and its GPS + time + heading do not repeat an already kept file (crops / re-uploads).

access_notes: Collected 2026-10-22 from a shared cloud IP. upload.wikimedia.org refused originals (429, Retry-After 600 s) at 00:31, 00:48, 00:55 and 01:05 UTC, so the final rule ran with --exif-source page and every photo has exif_source 'commons_page_metadata': the EXIF values of the description page's metadata table re-encoded with the product's EXIF writer (GPS to 0.01 arc-second, capture time to the minute, no GPSHPositioningError or MakerNote; checked against 16 original files by the fetcher: <= 0.1 m, <= 0.001 deg heading). Pixels are standard-width thumbnails (1920 px, smaller originals 1280 / 960 px) from thumb.wikimedia.org.

collection.note: distinct_requests = distinct URLs one clean run of the final rule needs (counted by an offline replay from the HTTP cache, which reproduced manifest.json byte for byte); live_* = every logged session that made requests, across rule versions and interrupted sessions (an upper bound on one clean run), at >= 1-2 s between requests.

schema_notes.format: Same layout as mdx-two-v1 (what scripts/benchmark.py reads): buildings[] with slug, name, centre {lat, lon}, centre_source, radius_m, osm_outline {file, sha256, licence, attribution, osm_url}, gt_reference {source, scene, component, archive_url, licence, sparse_files, images} and photos[] with key, title, file_name, file, sha256, exif_sha256, commons_page, original_url, thumbnail_width, author, author_url, licence, exif. Every other field is listed below.
schema_notes.paths: osm_outline.file is relative to the directory of testset.json (outlines/<slug>.geojson). photos[].file is relative to <cache-dir>/<testset_id>/<slug>/ after `python scripts/materialize_testset.py <testset_id> --cache-dir <cache-dir>` (= benchmark --data-root); the integrity report is <cache-dir>/<testset_id>/integrity_report.json and the reference models go to <cache-dir>/mdx/<slug>/<component>/sparse (--gt).
schema_notes.photo_extra: Extra per-photo fields: pixels_url (what is downloaded), pixels_sha256, orientation_reset, bytes/width/height of the materialised file, exif_source, original {width, height, mime, bytes}, credit, licence_url, sources (candidate lists that named the file), in_category.
schema_notes.building_extra: Extra per-building fields: name_zh, wikidata, commons_categories, shape_notes, osm_outline.osm_type/osm_id, stats, collect_params (fetch_commons_landmark arguments; input files by name only).
schema_notes.sha256: photos[].sha256 is the materialised file (thumbnail with the EXIF block grafted in); pixels_sha256 the downloaded thumbnail (or original) bytes; exif_sha256 the EXIF APP1 payload (starting with Exif\0\0) before the graft patched Orientation and pixel sizes. With exif_source 'original' that is the original's own EXIF block; with 'commons_page_metadata' it is fetch_commons_landmark.exif_from_page(exif_page_table). testset sha256 = sha256 of the testset.json bytes; outline and sparse files carry their own sha256.
schema_notes.exif: photos[].exif is what crowd3d.exif.read_photo_meta reads from the materialised file (lat/lon rounded to 1e-7 deg, others to 1e-3); null = absent. heading_ref 'T' true / 'M' magnetic north.
schema_notes.exif_page_table: Extra field: the MediaWiki EXIF table rows (text as rendered) the EXIF block is rebuilt from when exif_source is 'commons_page_metadata' (originals were not reachable when the set was collected). Absent for exif_source 'original'.
schema_notes.landmark_to_camera: Extra field: bearing/distance from the building centre to the EXIF GPS, the 8-sector index/label it falls in (crowd3d.coverage) and heading_offset_deg (0 = camera looks at the centre) when a heading exists.
schema_notes.gt_reference: Optional MegaDepth-X reference model (source 'megadepth-x'): scene, component (the one the curator chose), archive_url, sparse_files {name: {sha256, bytes}}, registered_images, photos_with_gt, archive_mb, and images = the image-name mapping {photo key: {name, name_in_megadepth_x, orientation}}. name is the image's exact name inside the sparse model's images.bin: name_in_megadepth_x (license.parquet) after '<scene>/<component>/images/' - '000123.jpg' in some scenes but 'commons/<subcat>/0/pictures/<file>' in others, so never reduce it to a basename. orientation = EXIF Orientation of the MegaDepth-X image the model was built from (its camera frame is the stored pixel grid; the materialised photos are upright), null when absent or invalid. Only photos registered in the model are mapped. additional_components (extra field): other components of the same scene, same layout (Brandenburg Gate west face); their photos carry gt_additional instead of gt_image.
schema_notes.key: photos[].key = the Commons file name (unique per building); what results and integrity rows use.
schema_notes.gt_image: Extra per-photo fields: gt_image / gt_orientation / name_in_megadepth_x repeat the gt_reference.images entry of the primary component; gt_additional {component, name, orientation, name_in_megadepth_x} marks a photo registered in an additional component.
schema_notes.dhash: Extra field: 64-bit dHash (crowd3d.validation.dhash_hex) of the thumbnail pixels; a re-rendered thumbnail within 4 bits counts as the same picture in the integrity report.
schema_notes.validation_at_freeze: Extra field: crowd3d.validation.validate_photo verdict at freeze time (code at the commit in 'created_with'). Informational: benchmarks re-run validation.
schema_notes.stats: Extra field per building: the collection funnel (listed, screened, EXIF/GPS counts) and summaries of the frozen photos (heading, focal, authors, sectors, GT overlap). last_collect_run is the collect run that wrote the manifest (often an offline replay from the HTTP cache: 0 requests); the live collection effort is under the top-level 'collection'.
schema_notes.selection: Extra top-level field: how candidates were screened and which photos were kept.
